 Sebastian Matta, a 19-year-old Democrat, won the race for Maricopa County Clerk of Superior Court on Tuesday. He speaks with Zach Prelutsky about his priorities By Zach Prelutsky Published : Nov. 6, 2026 at 8:58 PM MST | Updated : 9 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google PHOENIX (AZFamily) — Sebastian Matta , a 19-year-old Democrat, won the race for Maricopa County Clerk of Superior Court on Tuesday.
 Matta won 53% of the vote defeating former state Senator Jeff Dial, and the days since have been busy.
 He credited Democrats’ strong showing in the midterms and his own campaigning over the last several months for the win.
 “It’s certainly been exciting. It’s much more of a bigger result than I expected when I originally won,” Matta said.
 Since his victory, Matta has appeared on late-night talk shows, and national publications have profiled him. After an interview with Arizona’s Family on Friday, he had to leave for another one he had scheduled.
 “We’re just middle-of-the-road Americans. My parents immigrated to this country in the early 2000s, and I think I’m just a relatable person,” Matta said.
 Matta will lead about 670 employees as the Clerk of Superior Court. Some have worked in the office since before his parents were born.
 “I hope that they realize that I’m just not any 19-year-old,” Matta said.
 The Clerk of Superior Court retains, secures and stores every court record in Maricopa County. The office processes roughly 16,000 documents a day.
 Matta was first introduced to the office as a toddler when he would accompany his dad, who is a car crash investigator, to the clerk’s office to pick up various documents.
 “I believe that if you are running for public office and you don’t firmly believe in your capabilities, I think that you probably shouldn’t be running for public office,” Matta said.
 Matta wants to expand language access and move more court services, including initiating probate matters, online. When he starts in his new elected position, he plans on spending the first part getting to know the staff before implementing the changes.
 “This isn’t a stepping stone for me. This is just something I have a deep-seated passion about, and I hope that the voters can recognize that,” Matta said. “I know my stuff, and I’m hoping that anybody who thinks that they may have taken a gamble on me, I hope that they realize that their gamble will hopefully pay off.”
